chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, hates the notoriety/ostentation of clothing.

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — a divine epithet used to glorify God, often abbreviated 'SWT'
key_terms.شُهْرَةَ اللِّبَاسِ: Notoriety/ostentation of dress — clothing worn to attract attention or stand out, whether through extravagance or conspicuous austerity
key_terms.يُبْغِضُ: Hates/abhors — a strong expression indicating divine dislike, stronger than mere disapproval

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about wearing clothing to show off or attract attention?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that Allah abhors shuhrat al-libas — clothing worn for the purpose of drawing attention, ostentation, or social display. This concise hadith establishes a key principle of Islamic dress ethics: the intent behind clothing matters, and seeking fame or notoriety through dress is displeasing to God. Historically, this teaching addressed both extremes — wearing excessively fine clothes for display of wealth, and wearing conspicuously coarse garments for display of piety.
